fichas.title: Footpaths and Cycle Ways
fichas.summary: Guidance for pedestrian and cycle routes emphasizes varied, interesting walking areas, weather protection, and adequate widths and safety separation. Combined footpaths and cycleways are also referenced to page 384.

dimensions.label: Roadside pavement width
dimensions.context: Recommended minimum width if possible; includes a minimum 1.50 m walking width and 0.50 m safety distance from the carriageway.
dimensions.ocr_raw:
Roadside pavements should if possible not
be narrower than 2 m (of which 1.50 m min. width and 0.50 m
safety distance from the carriageway).

dimensions.label: Minimum walking width within roadside pavement
dimensions.context: Minimum width stated as part of the roadside pavement recommendation.
dimensions.ocr_raw: 1.50 m min. width

dimensions.label: Safety distance from carriageway
dimensions.context: Safety distance included in the roadside pavement recommendation.
dimensions.ocr_raw:
0.50 m
safety distance from the carriageway

dimensions.label: Ideal minimum pavement width near schools and other facilities
dimensions.context: Near schools, shopping centres, leisure facilities, etc.
dimensions.ocr_raw:
Near schools, shopping centres,
leisure facilities etc., a min. width of 3 m is ideal.

dimensions.label: Roadside cycleway width, one-way traffic
dimensions.context: Minimum width for one-way cycle traffic.
dimensions.ocr_raw:

traffic

dimensions.label: Roadside cycleway width, two-way traffic
dimensions.context: Stated width for two-way cycle traffic; minimum width is listed separately.

dimensions.context: Minimum width for two-way cycle traffic.

fichas.title: Road Cross-Sections and Design Parameters
fichas.summary: A design-parameter table accompanies diagrams of pedestrian and cycle traffic areas. It gives road-related parameters including curve radii, longitudinal slope, rounded brow and dip radii, and minimum clear height. Bracketed values indicate minimum dimensions in existing built-up areas; some dimensions are identified as exceptional cases.
